description:
What the OWOX Data Marts Shopify connector loads from a store through the Shopify Admin GraphQL API, and how the tables fit together. The commerce core is Orders, Customers, Products and Product Variants: an order points to its customer, a variant to its product and to its inventory item, and money movements (Tender Transactions) and shipments (Fulfillment Orders) point back to the order. Fulfillment Orders also point to the Locations they ship from. Abandoned Checkouts record the customers who started and did not finish an order.

The store's content is Blogs, Articles and Pages. Ten metafield tables, one per owner type, hold the custom fields merchants and apps attach to blogs, articles, pages, products, variants, collections, customers, orders, locations and the shop; each points to its owner on `ownerId`.

Every id is a Shopify global ID, a string such as `gid://shopify/Order/…`. Order and customer detail without a column of its own (line items, shipping lines, refunds, discount codes) is kept as JSON text, to unnest in SQL.
questions: How do orders, refunds and discounts add up to net sales per month and per customer?
Which customers placed repeat orders, and which started a checkout they never finished?
Which products and variants sell, and what stock record and location stand behind them?

Orders.description:
One row per order placed in the store: financial and fulfillment status, order totals (subtotal, tax, shipping, discounts, refunded), currency, customer contact fields, billing and shipping location, tags, source and the key timestamps. Detail that has no column of its own is kept as JSON text: the line items, shipping lines, refunds, discount codes and the customer object.

This is the table most questions start from. `customerId` points to Customers, and Fulfillment Orders, Tender Transactions and Order Metafields point back here on the order `id`. The `id` is Shopify's global ID, a string such as `gid://shopify/Order/…`, not a number.
questions: What were net sales, tax and shipping per month, and how much of it was refunded?
Which discount codes brought in the most revenue, and what share of orders used one?
How many orders sit in each financial and fulfillment status, and how old is the oldest unfulfilled one?

Customers.description:
One row per customer account: name, email, phone, account state, locale, marketing consent for email and SMS, number of orders, lifetime spend, tags and default address. `amountSpent` is a JSON string holding the amount and its currency code.

Orders and Abandoned Checkouts point here on `customerId`. A guest checkout can have an order without a customer row, so a join from Orders to Customers is a left join.
questions: How many customers placed one order, two orders, or more, and what did each group spend?
Which countries do customers with email marketing consent live in?
How many customers were created each month, and how many of them have ordered?

Products.description:
One row per product in the catalog: title, handle, vendor, product type, status, tags, total inventory, number of variants, the lowest and highest variant price, SEO title and description, and publication and update times. Prices live on the variants; this table holds the range.

Product Variants and Product Metafields point here on the product `id`.
questions: Which vendors and product types have the most active products?
Which active products have no inventory left?
How many products were published each month, and which are still drafts?

Product Variants.description:
One row per product variant, the sellable unit: title, SKU, barcode, price, compare-at price, position, inventory quantity and policy, tax settings and availability. It names its product (`productId`, `productTitle`) and its inventory item (`inventoryItemId`).

Use it to move from a product to its SKUs and prices, and from a SKU to its stock record in Inventory Items.
questions: How many variants does each product have, and what is the price spread inside a product?
Which variants are available for sale but have zero inventory quantity?
Which variants are priced below their compare-at price, and by how much?

Inventory Items.description:
One row per inventory item, the stock-keeping record behind a variant: SKU, whether stock is tracked, whether it requires shipping, harmonized system code and country of origin, with creation and update times. Stock quantities per location are not in this table.

Product Variants point here on `inventoryItemId`; `variantId` here names the variant the item belongs to.
questions: Which inventory items are not tracked, and which of them require shipping?
Which countries of origin appear most often across inventory items?
Which items have no harmonized system code?

Collections.description:
One row per collection: title, handle, description, sort order, template suffix, number of products, image URL and last update. Which products belong to a collection is not a column here, so this table describes collections but does not list their members.

Collection Metafields point here on the collection `id`.
questions: Which collections hold the most products?
Which collections were updated most recently?
How are collections sorted, and how many use each sort order?

Discount Codes.description:
One row per discount code: the code, discount type, title, status, start and end time, usage limit, whether it applies once per customer and the number of uses counted asynchronously. The codes customers actually used on an order are kept as JSON text in Orders (`discountCodes`).

There is no key column to join this table to Orders; match on the `code` text inside the JSON.
questions: Which discount codes are active now, and which expire this month?
How many codes of each discount type exist?
Which codes are close to their usage limit?

Abandoned Checkouts.description:
Checkouts that a customer started and did not complete: recovery URL, completion time, line item quantity, total price, billing and shipping location, and the customer's name and email. `totalPriceSet` is a JSON string with the amount and currency.

Use it for recovery campaigns and for the gap between started and completed checkouts. `customerId` points to Customers and may be empty when the checkout came from a draft order or an app.
questions: How many checkouts were abandoned each week, and what was their total value?
Which countries have the most abandoned checkouts?
How many abandoned checkouts belong to customers who have ordered before?

Shop.description:
One row for the store: name, email, domains, currency, time zone, weight unit, billing address, plan, whether taxes are included in prices, and creation and update times. It is where to read the store currency and time zone.

Shop Metafields point here on the shop `id`.
questions: Which currency, time zone and plan is the store set up with?
Are taxes included in prices, and is shipping taxed?
What is the store's primary domain and billing country?

Locations.description:
One row per location, physical or virtual: name, whether it is active, primary, a fulfillment service location, whether it fulfills online orders, holds active inventory or ships inventory, with address, phone and times.

Fulfillment Orders point here on `assignedLocationId`, and Location Metafields on the location `id`.
questions: Which locations are active and fulfill online orders?
Which locations hold active inventory but do not ship it?
How many locations are there per country?

Fulfillment Orders.description:
One row per fulfillment order, the instruction to ship part of an order from one location: status, request status, the order (`orderId`, `orderName`), the assigned location (`assignedLocationId`, `assignedLocationName`), fulfill-at time, delivery method and timestamps. One order can have several fulfillment orders when it ships from several places.

Use it to follow an order from placement to shipment.
questions: How many fulfillment orders are open, in progress or closed, and which locations hold the open ones?
How long do fulfillment orders take from creation to closing, per location?
Which orders were split into more than one fulfillment order?

Tender Transactions.description:
One row per tender transaction, an actual movement of money between buyer and shop: amount, currency, remote payment reference, whether it is a test transaction, the order it belongs to and the time it was processed. Shopify describes it as the record to use for reconciling payments.

Orders is the table to join: `orderId` is empty when the order has been deleted.
questions: How much money moved per day, by currency, excluding test transactions?
Which orders have no tender transaction?
How many test transactions are mixed into the data?

Blogs.description:
One row per blog of the online store: title, handle, template suffix, creation and update times. A blog holds articles.

Articles point here on `blogId`, and Blog Metafields on the blog `id`.
questions: How many blogs does the store have, and when was each last updated?
Which blogs use a custom template?
Which blog was created first?

Articles.description:
One row per blog article: title, handle, body, summary, author name, the blog it sits in (`blogId`, `blogTitle`), whether it is published, publication time, tags, template suffix, image URL and timestamps.

Use it to count content output per blog and author.
questions: How many articles were published per blog and month?
Which authors wrote the most articles?
Which articles are still unpublished, and since when?

Pages.description:
One row per static page of the online store: title, handle, body, body summary, publication status and time, template suffix and timestamps.

Page Metafields point here on the page `id`.
questions: Which pages are unpublished?
Which pages changed most recently?
How many pages use a custom template?

Blog Metafields.description:
One row per metafield attached to blogs: namespace, key, value, type, and the owner (`ownerId`, `ownerType`) with creation and update times. A metafield is a custom field a merchant or app adds to a Shopify resource; its value is stored as text whatever its type.

`ownerId` is the `id` of the row in Blogs that the metafield belongs to. The connector reads the first 250 metafields per owner.
questions: Which metafield namespaces and keys exist on blogs, and how many rows does each have?
Which blogs have a given metafield set, and to what value?

joins.note: The customer who started the checkout; may be empty.
joins.source: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2026-07/objects/AbandonedCheckout (customer: "The customer who created this checkout. May be null if the checkout was created from a draft order or via an app.")

joins.note: The product the variant belongs to.

joins.note: The stock record behind the variant. Each variant has one inventory item, so the join does not repeat rows.
